text:
Maya (Support): heads up — customer 'BrightLeaf' hit us with repeated streaming disconnects during long responses. They say sessions close mid-stream and client sees 'connection reset by peer' after ~45s of slow consumption. trace=tx-9f3b

Aisha (SRE): can you paste the customer's minimal repro and any server logs? sounds like slow-consumer backpressure but need data :thinking:

Maya (Support): repro steps they gave:
```
# client: slow reader
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/resp?model=xlarge
# They then sleep 40s before reading first chunk
sleep 40 && tail -c +1 stream.out
```
They also captured proxy logs attached (snippet below).

oncall-bot: incident RINF-2026-03-05-7 created (priority: P2). link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-12345

Carlos (Platform Eng): paste of proxy stdout around tx-9f3b:
```
[2026-03-05T12:12:21.342Z] tx-9f3b write 65536 bytes -> 0 (EAGAIN)
[2026-03-05T12:12:21.342Z] tx-9f3b write 65536 bytes -> -1 (EPIPE)
[2026-03-05T12:12:21.343Z] tx-9f3b connection aborted, code=SOCKET_ABORT, backlog=42
```
Suggests kernel dropped write when client unread.

Jesse (Client Eng): is the client using a single-threaded event loop? most libs will buffer in userland but kernel sndbuf is finite; if writes block we'll see EAGAIN then EPIPE if socket closed. what are their client lib and OS?

Maya (Support): they're on node 18 using axios + eventsource-polyfill inside an electron app. they said the app can be paused (tab hidden) which delays reads.

Aisha (SRE): hypothesis: large first-frame + streaming delta causes kernel buffer to fill; when the app pauses reading, proxy keeps trying to write entire chunk; behind TCP that leads to EAGAIN then abort path in our runtime after configured write retry window. Need to confirm: what's our write retry policy on the streaming path? Carlos?

Carlos (Platform Eng): current runtime: attempts nonblocking write; if EAGAIN we queue in runtime in-memory buffer up to 4MB per-connection, then retry for up to 30s before forcibly aborting. However we also have a 'soft_limit' at 1.2MB where we stop coalescing and start dropping larger frames to keep SLOs. I see backlog=42 in log (multiple pending requests).

Nina (Support): customer says partial tokens are arriving (first 512 bytes) then silence, then eventually socket dies. they also forwarded a pcap showing retransmits then RST.

Aisha (SRE): next steps for repro: 1) reproduce with a slow reader locally using our curl approach; 2) capture runtime logs with debug write_flow and socket stats; 3) try changing per-conn send buffer and our per-conn queue cap to isolate whether limit hits before socket closed. i'll attempt repro on staging in 10m.

Jesse (Client Eng): also ask customer to try setting TCP_NODELAY and lowering their read chunk interval. In electron, the event loop pause may block JS read callbacks — suggest a native streaming client or unpausing the tab.

Carlos (Platform Eng): quick check on staging: increased per-conn buffer to 8MB and repro script produced longer survival (90s) but eventually same EPIPE when client delays >120s. logs show queue grew to 7.3MB then kernel refused.

Maya (Support): pinged customer with two workarounds: (a) adopt client streaming consumer that keeps draining even when tab hidden, (b) use shorter initial chunks from server (flush earlier) — customer responded they can try (a) but slow to change app. :thumbsup:

Aisha (SRE): short-term mitigation: reduce per-write frame sizes on server for streaming path to 4KB chunks with 10ms flush. This keeps buffer pressure lower and will provide partial tokens incrementally so paused clients won't see huge single-write bursts. We'll A/B toggle for a subset of hosts.

Carlos (Platform Eng): implementation note: add config feature 'stream.flush_chunk_bytes' and 'stream.flush_interval_ms' and gate behind rollout. Also add metric 'conn.outstanding_bytes' to alert earlier.

Maya (Support): customer asked whether billing or auth could be related — they saw 502 then 401 on retries. any correlation?

Aisha (SRE): unlikely. 401 likely from token expiry on retry path, 502 is our abort error when runtime kills connection. We'll surface clearer status codes in client path (add a 'stream_closed_due_to_backpressure' code) so customers can programmatically retry with fresh token.

Jesse (Client Eng): repro notes i pushed to the internal gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/stream-slow-repro — includes node/electron tweaks, and a tiny Go client that keeps a separate reader thread.

Carlos (Platform Eng): rolling canary with 4KB flush now on staging. initial telemetry: median conn.outstanding_bytes dropped from 0.9MB -> 48KB, disconnects due to SOCKET_ABORT down 78% for canary shard.

Maya (Support): shared workarounds with BrightLeaf. they're testing the client change while we watch the canary. will update when they confirm. :rotating_light:

Nina (Support): filed follow-up email template for customers hit by this: short explanation, two mitigation steps (client keep-alive / server chunking), and link to docs + support contact. added to the ticket.

Aisha (SRE): longer-term: evaluate server-side backpressure propagation to client (SSE keepalive with backpressure hint) and better queue-shedding policy (prioritize small frames). Also add an entry in the runbook under "streaming slow-consumer" with metrics thresholds.

Maya (Support): thanks all. I'll post a customer-facing summary after BrightLeaf confirms. thread closed for now but will reopen if they see more failures. :white_check_mark:
